decisions.title: Adopt the proposal as a whole
decisions.summary: The proposal to make the buffer protocol accessible in Python was accepted, with the decision to drop the distinction between mutable and immutable buffers.
decisions.rationale: The discussion concluded that distinguishing mutable vs. immutable buffers was not necessary, and the PEP was simplified for the sake of clarity and usefulness in typing.

evidence.quote: I decided to give up on distinguishing mutable vs. immutable buffers for now, especially because Introspection and "mutable XOR shared" semantics for PyBuffer may give us a more robust way to tell them apart in the future. This will make the PEP simpler but still useful for typing.
evidence.author: Jelle

decisions.title: When to call `__release_buffer__`
decisions.summary: The decision is still open on when to call `__release_buffer__` and whether it should be called manually or handled by the memoryview.
decisions.rationale: The participants are discussing the necessity and feasibility of enforcing the call to `__release_buffer__` through `memoryview(..., exporter=self)` to avoid potential issues with manual buffer management.

evidence.quote: Currently it’s not clear to me when to call `__release_buffer__` vs. when a wrapper or memoryview does it for you: e.g. the PEP says “It is also possible to call `__release_buffer__` on a C class that implements `bf_releasebuffer`” – when should you do it, and what happens if you should do it but don’t (and vice versa)?
evidence.author: encukou

evidence.quote: FWIW, when I get time I want to check if the following would be a better (simpler/safer) approach:
evidence.author: encukou

evidence.quote: You should call it when you want to release a memoryview you got from a call to `__buffer__`. It’s probably going to be very rarely necessary, because you can just do `with obj.__buffer__(flags)` and the memoryview’s `__exit__` method will call the buffer for you.
evidence.author: Jelle

evidence.quote: If you call `__buffer__` directly, you’re on your own. I see this as similar to the context manager protocol: `__enter__` and `__exit__` should be called in pairs, but if you call `__enter__` directly and don’t call `__exit__`, the runtime isn’t going to call it for you.

decisions.title: Introduce a new Python API for memoryview(..., exporter=self)
decisions.summary: The proposal to introduce a new Python API for `memoryview(..., exporter=self)` was rejected.
decisions.rationale: Jelle prefers to avoid introducing new Python APIs if possible, citing the costs associated with documentation, bikeshedding, and reasoning about correctness. The lack of a clear benefit to enforcing this in `__buffer__` was also noted.

evidence.quote: I’d be open to adding new Python APIs if that’s helpful, but every new Python API has some cost (documentation, bikeshedding over naming/semantics, having to reason about correctness if it’s used in unexpected ways). So I’d prefer to avoid introducing a new Python API if possible.
evidence.author: Jelle
